findings.title: Keep client certificates out of the shared SSL context
findings.why_it_matters: A request that supplies a client certificate can cause later default-verified requests, including those from other sessions, to present that certificate to another server. urllib3 loads the client certificate into the supplied SSLContext, so sharing the global context also allows concurrent requests using different certificates to overwrite each other's identity. Use a separate context when a client certificate is supplied to preserve per-request identity isolation.
findings.suggested_fix: Only reuse the preloaded context for requests without a client certificate; give client-certificate requests a separate context with the default CA bundle, and test sequential and concurrent mTLS isolation.
evidence:
src/requests/adapters.py:94-95 -- elif verify is True:
        pool_kwargs["ssl_context"] = _preloaded_ssl_context
src/requests/adapters.py:102-105 -- if client_cert is not None: ... pool_kwargs["cert_file"] = client_cert[0]
tests/test_requests.py:2959-2962 covers client certificates with verify=False and a failed default-verified handshake, not the shared context's identity isolation.

testing_gaps: No test exercises concurrent default-verified HTTPS requests or checks that they reuse preloaded CA certificates without reloading the bundle; the stated performance objective can regress without detection.
